head: c8cb37a
target: check(run) judges a run so an engine bug and a model mistake no longer look alike: invariants pass or fail and never skip, behaviors are rates over the trials that had a chance, and cost is reported but never judged.
incidental: cost arithmetic: token sums, ratio rounding and per-step request grouping
the JSON-path walker that visits every string and key for secret-free
tool-name parsing: the plugin is the part before the double underscore
test plumbing: the faux scripts, the log mutation helpers and the pick evidence helper

questions.prompt: The live test used to assert three ad hoc properties and log the rest, so an engine bug and a model mistake looked alike. Why does check judge a run as two classes, invariants and behaviors?

options.label: Invariants are checked without a model, so they are free, while behaviors need a paid run.
An invariant is an engine property every trial must keep, so one failure is an engine bug; a behavior is a bet on the model, measured as a rate, so one failure is a data point.
Invariants hold in native tool mode and behaviors in dispatch mode.
Invariants guard secrets and behaviors guard plugins.

key_points: a failing invariant names an engine bug the engine must fix
a failing behavior is a data point in a rate about the model, not a bug
the split exists because the old live test could not tell the two apart

questions.prompt: A model answers both weather prompts without ever enabling the weather plugin. The report shows discover@1 fail and use@1 skip. What does the skip mean for use's rate?

options.label: The trial counts as a fail, because ignoring the tool is what the check bets against.
The trial counts as a pass, because the model cannot be blamed for what never ran.
use had no chance to show, so the trial is left out of the rate; only trials where the model enabled the plugin count.
The whole run drops out of every behavior's rate.

key_points: a skip is left out of the behavior's rate
a behavior skips when its precondition never happened, here the model never enabling the plugin
discover still fails on the same run, so the model is judged where it had a chance

questions.prompt: Months from now, the multeval grader needs aigent's verdicts on stored runs. Where does it get them, and what does it not need?

options.label: It reads a result directory back into a run log and runs check on it; it needs no engine, session or model, and it gets the verdict the live test and the CLI would.
It runs the scenario again with a cheap model, because a run log is only valid live.
It reimplements the checks over the raw transcript, because check is live-test code.
It subscribes to session events and grades them as they stream.

key_points: check reads only the run log, so a stored result directory grades offline
every caller, the live test, the CLI and the grader, gets the same verdict from the same files
the grader needs no engine, session or model

questions.prompt: check reads the transcript and the step events together. Which of these would it lose or misjudge if it saw only the events and never the transcript?

options.label: The plugins a session started with: no listener can subscribe before the session is returned, so calls to them would look like enabled-before-call violations.
The plugins the model enabled during a prompt: those arrive only as transcript records.
A core__call_tool that was rejected before it ran: it leaves no tool event, only an error result in the transcript.
The final answer of a prompt: the transcript is the only place it is kept.

key_points: a session's creation records reach no listener, so its enabled-at-start set is read from the transcript
a rejected core__call_tool leaves an error result in the transcript and no tool event, which dispatch-recover needs
tool outcomes and turn ends live in the events, so the two sources are merged, not chosen between

questions.prompt: Two runs of the same scenario pass every behavior. One used ten times the tokens of the other. What does the report say about that?

options.label: The expensive run fails a cost check, so cost is capped like a behavior.
The cost numbers appear in the report with no verdict attached; cost is reported to explain results, never judged, because cheap is not correctness.
The report leaves cost out, because tokens are an engine detail.
The expensive run's behaviors are skipped, because a costly model cannot be trusted.

key_points: cost is reported as numbers and never judged: no verdict keys on it
the verdicts are about correctness; cost is measurement for later analysis, such as the model comparison

questions.prompt: A new behavior check, clarify, arrives: the model must ask the user a question before it calls a tool. Where does it go in this design, and what stops it shipping unjudged or untested?
key_points: a scenario parser entry: its fields and the names it references, so scenarios can declare it
a judge case in checks.ts: the judge switch is exhaustive, so a check without a judge fails the build
a case in the test table, which is typed by the check names, so it ships with a passing and a failing case
it must own its precondition and its skip rule

questions.prompt: No model script can make a correct engine break an invariant. How does the test suite give each invariant a failing case?

options.label: It scripts the faux model to misbehave until the invariant trips.
It takes a correct run, injects one fault that stands for a named engine bug, and asserts the failing verdict's evidence names that bug.
It runs the engine with a buggy plugin until the invariant trips.
It builds the run log by hand, with no run behind it.

key_points: an invariant is an engine property, so no model script can break it on a correct engine
the failing case is a correct run with one injected fault, named for the engine bug it stands for
the passing case's evidence shows the invariant was exercised, so the pass is not vacuous

questions.prompt: check meets a transcript message it does not know: an unknown role, or a known role with unexpected content. What does it do, and what would ignoring the message cost?

options.label: It throws, because a check over a misread transcript would be wrong without saying so; ignoring would silently turn a misread into a wrong verdict.
It skips the message and judges the rest, because one odd message should not sink a report.
It reads the message as a system message, the one role with no content to misread.
It fails every invariant, because an unknown message proves the engine is broken.

key_points: an unknown or malformed message makes check throw
ignoring would silently produce a wrong verdict
the strictness keeps the checks honest when the transcript shape changes

questions.prompt: use skips when the model never enables the tool's plugin. host-enable has no skip for a host that never enables. Why the difference?

options.label: Host enables are recorded in a shape the check cannot see.
host-enable is an invariant, and invariants never skip.
The scenario format promises host-enable its enable step, and the parser rejects the scenario without it before any paid run; what the model does mid-run cannot be promised, so that becomes a skip.
A host that never enables is not a mistake, so there is nothing to judge.

key_points: setup the scenario format can promise is enforced at authoring time, before a paid run
preconditions that depend on what the model or the run did become skips
the run log carries the scenario, so a stored run keeps the same guarantee

questions.prompt: check grades a stored result directory from a paid run. The report shows secret-free fail, use@1 skip, follow@1 fail, and every other invariant pass. Which of these hold?

options.label: The engine let a raw secret value into the run log's data; the scrub replaced it with a mark, and that mark is the evidence.
use@1's trial is left out of use's rate, because its precondition never happened.
The scrub is broken: it should have removed every trace of the secret before check ran.
follow@1's failure is a data point about the model's answer, not an engine bug.

key_points: a failing invariant names an engine bug, whatever the model did
a skip leaves the rate, and a behavior failure is the model's data point
grading the stored files works because check reads only the run log
